items.summary: Risk disposition: blocked for public launch and rights-dependent monetization; conditional for ordinary reversible work that preserves existing consent, disclosures, provenance, claims, copyright/trademark, platform-policy, and data boundaries. Exact decision: keep searchwoot.com private, reject the proposed dumbsluts.com dispatch, retain parked-site dispositions, and continue only existing read-only evidence, measurement, attribution, failure-repair, and security work. Evidence: Woot public terms do not establish public/commercial redistribution rights; 0 of 4 launch-readiness legal tasks are closed; accuracy/freshness, security, and measurement gates are blocked; compliance is technical-only with 37 pass, 15 fail, and 7 unknown; analytics has 39 configured sites with source-permission errors; revenue covers 2026-09-21 only and includes $4.92 aggregate unattributed commission. No go-live proposal is supported.

Launch-readiness tracking remains active at 0 of 4 tasks closed. No task is closable on current evidence. Open tasks: searchwoot-legal-source-rights, searchwoot-data-flow-retention, searchwoot-ga4-consent-evidence, and searchwoot-logs-vendors-incident. Progress is limited to existing public terms, API documentation, repository/configuration artifacts, and privacy/cookie pages; these do not satisfy the completion rule. Next evidence action: attach the consolidated read-only bundle and field-level rights matrix covering provenance, permitted storage, caching, display, derivatives, alerts, attribution, freshness, correction, takedown, identifiers, retention, deletion, access, notification consent, unsubscribe behavior, GA4 settings, log fields, vendor coverage, and incident/request procedures.

Data-use dispositions: Woot API deal and price-history data is counsel_required; user alert rules and sync results are evidence_needed; GA4 analytics is evidence_needed; operational logs and Cloudflare hosting data are evidence_needed. No item is clear for public or monetized use.

Do not block ordinary growth solely because telemetry is incomplete. However, concrete compliance failures must be remediated before exposure or monetization. Current evidence supports technical compliance only, not certification; revenue and ROI claims remain unsupported because the $4.92 provider aggregate cannot be assigned to a site and cost periods do not align.
